title: High-Performance Eigensolver Combining EigenExa and Iterative Refinement
problem: When eigenvalues are narrowly clustered, eigenvector computation becomes ill-posed, resulting in inaccurate and unreliable eigenpairs. Standard eigensolvers may fail to provide sufficiently accurate results in such scenarios.
motivation: Eigenvalue decomposition is ubiquitous in scientific simulations, and obtaining reliable, accurate eigenvectors is critical for simulation correctness and trustworthiness.
method: The approach combines mixed-precision iterative refinement with EigenExa, a modern high-performance eigensolver. It employs both ordinary and highly-accurate precisions to iteratively refine eigenvectors computed by the base solver, improving accuracy without requiring expensive arbitrary precision arithmetic. EigenExa handles the initial large-scale eigendecomposition with high parallelism across distributed memory systems.
key_novelty: Applying mixed-precision iterative refinement to improve eigenvector accuracy in clustered eigenvalue scenarios, eliminating the need for arbitrary precision eigensolvers.
contributions: Mixed-precision iterative refinement methods for improving eigenvector accuracy and reliability
Integration of iterative refinement with EigenExa for high-performance and scalable eigensolving
Demonstration that mixed-precision refinement achieves accuracy improvements without expensive arbitrary precision computations
Numerical validation of accuracy and performance on large-scale parallel systems
